resources.string: Answers are written by AI on DLNE\'s own server. If it is restarting or down, a computer that someone lends to DLNE may answer instead. Photos you add go to DLNE\'s own server to write the answer and are never sent to a lent computer. Like every message, they are processed by the shared model, whose layers can run on lent graphics cards; those cards see only intermediate numbers, never the picture. DLNE doesn\'t keep them. Answers can be slow and can be wrong. Don\'t send passwords, private details or anything secret.

Off unless you turn it on, here or by saying yes when DLNE asks in a chat. When you ask something local (near me, nearby, the weather), your phone\'s precise location goes with that message to DLNE\'s own server, only for lookups that need it: local weather (rounded to about 100 m, sent to Open-Meteo) and local searches (only a nearby place name). Other questions never use it. The AI model never gets your coordinates, only the town named in those lookups\' results. Nothing is logged or stored. If your phone can\'t find its position within a few seconds, the message goes without it and the app tells you.
Location permission was refused, so sharing stays off. You can allow it in Android\'s app settings.

DLNE has no accounts, and this app collects nothing about you: no analytics, no ads, no tracking. The one exception is location, which is off unless you turn it on. If you do, your phone\'s precise location is sent with a local question (near me, nearby, the weather) to DLNE\'s own server and is used only for lookups that need it. For local weather, the coordinates, rounded to about 100 m, go to the weather service (Open-Meteo). For local searches, only a nearby place name is added to the search, which DLNE\'s search sends to web search engines. The AI model that answers never gets your coordinates; when it looks something up near you, the results it reads name the nearby town. Your location is never logged or stored.

Your chats are stored only on this phone. When you send a message, the conversation so far travels over an encrypted connection to the DLNE service, which passes it to DLNE\'s own server to write the answer. Only if that server is restarting or down, it may pass it to a computer that someone lends to DLNE instead.

Photos you add go to DLNE\'s own server to write the answer and are never sent to a lent computer. Like every message, they are processed by the shared model, whose layers can run on lent graphics cards; those cards see only intermediate numbers, never the picture. DLNE doesn\'t keep them. Your newest photos go again with the messages after them, so the AI can still see them. They stay on this phone with the chat, so deleting the chat deletes them. The phone takes the camera details and location out of a photo before it sends it.

When you ask for a picture, the description the AI writes for it goes to DLNE\'s own server, which checks it, draws the picture on its own computer and keeps it in memory for up to 30 minutes after it is made, so your phone can collect it. The picture is kept on this phone with the chat.

A lent computer belongs to someone else, so don\'t send passwords, private details or anything secret, in case yours is answered by one. The service sees your network (IP) address, which it uses to limit how often each network can ask.
Lookups (weather, Wikipedia, news, web search) are made by the DLNE server, not your phone; reported answers are kept on the server for review.
Every chat stored on this phone will be removed. This can\'t be undone.
